# Arroz con Pollo Norteño 🇲🇽

::: {.dish-meta}
**Region:** Northern Mexico (Sonora & Chihuahua)  ·  **Family:** One-pot pilaf (*arroz rojo* base)
**Serves:** 4–6  ·  **Active time:** 45 minutes  ·  **Total:** 1 hour 10 min
**Assembly:** 🍲 Cooked together — chicken browned, then rice cooked in the same pot
:::

Not to be confused with its [Caribbean-Spanish cousin](arroz-con-pollo.qmd) a few
pages back: the northern-Mexican version is built on **arroz rojo** — Mexican red
rice — with a tomato-forward base, a hit of cumin and Mexican oregano, a whole
green chile for perfume, and (if you're doing it right) a splash of cold lager.
It's *cocina norteña* comfort food, the kind that lands on the table on a Sunday
in Hermosillo or Chihuahua.

## The story

Northern Mexico is ranch country — big skies, cattle, flour tortillas, and hearty,
unfussy cooking. Its arroz con pollo grows out of **arroz rojo**, the everyday
red rice that anchors Mexican home tables, which itself descends from the same
Spanish rice tradition (carried across the Pacific on the Manila galleon and
planted in colonial kitchens) that produced *arroz con pollo* all over Latin
America.

What makes the *norteño* take its own dish is the accent: no sofrito, olives, or
achiote here. Instead there's a smooth blended tomato base fried until it darkens,
warm cumin and **Mexican oregano** (brighter and more citrusy than the
Mediterranean kind), a fresh serrano or jalapeño, and the region's habit of
deglazing with a **cerveza**. It's finished with lime, cilantro, avocado, and a
stack of warm tortillas.

## Ingredients

**Chicken**

- 1 kg (2.2 lb) bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks
- ½ tsp ground cumin, ½ tsp Mexican oregano, salt and pepper
- 2 tbsp neutral oil (or lard, the traditional — and dairy-free — norteño fat)

**Red-rice base**

- 3 Roma tomatoes, quartered
- ¼ white onion (plus ½ onion, diced, for the pot)
- 2 cloves garlic
- 300 g (1.5 cups) long-grain white rice, rinsed until nearly clear and **drained well**
- 1 carrot, diced
- 1 small potato, diced (optional, very norteño)
- 80 g (½ cup) peas and/or corn kernels
- 1 whole serrano or jalapeño (left whole for aroma; slit and diced if you want heat)
- ½ tsp cumin, pinch Mexican oregano
- ~600 ml (2.5 cups) chicken broth
- 120 ml (½ cup) Mexican lager (optional; reduce the broth by the same amount)
- Salt

**To serve:** chopped cilantro, lime wedges, sliced avocado, warm corn tortillas,
and a simple tomato-chile salsa

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Gluten-free · dairy-free:** naturally both — rice, chicken, tomato, and oil (or
lard). Two things to watch: use a **certified gluten-free, dairy-free chicken
bouillon** if you're not using homemade broth (Mexican brands like Knorr Suiza
often contain wheat and/or milk), and serve with **corn tortillas** rather than the
region's usual wheat flour ones (or a gluten-free tortilla). Confirm your beer is
gluten-free, or just leave it out.
:::

## Method

1. Pat the chicken dry and season with cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper. In a wide
   heavy pot or *cazuela*, brown the pieces well in the oil on all sides. Remove
   and set aside — they'll finish in the rice.
2. Meanwhile, blend the tomatoes, onion quarter, and garlic with a splash of the
   broth into a smooth purée. Set aside.
3. Lower the heat to medium. Add the **drained rice** to the same pot (add a little
   more oil if needed) and toast, stirring often, until the grains turn golden and
   smell nutty, 5–6 minutes. Stir in the diced onion and carrot for the last 2
   minutes. *This toasting step is what keeps the grains separate and gives arroz
   rojo its flavor — don't skip it.*
4. Pour in the blended tomato base (stand back — it will splatter). Fry, stirring,
   3–4 minutes until it darkens to a deep brick red and the raw-tomato smell is
   gone.
5. Add the broth (and beer, if using), cumin, oregano, potato, peas/corn, and the
   whole chile. Season with salt — the liquid should taste well seasoned. Nestle
   the chicken and any resting juices back in.
6. Bring to a boil, then cover, drop to the **lowest heat, and cook 18–20 minutes**
   without stirring, until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.
7. Kill the heat and let it rest, covered, 10 minutes. Fish out the whole chile,
   fluff gently with a fork, and finish with cilantro, a good squeeze of lime, and
   avocado. Serve straight from the pot with warm tortillas and salsa.

## The norteño difference

Three moves set this apart from the [Caribbean-Spanish version](arroz-con-pollo.qmd):

- **A blended, fried tomato base** (*arroz rojo*) instead of a diced sofrito —
  smoother, deeper, brick-red.
- **Cumin + Mexican oregano + fresh green chile** instead of saffron, olives, and
  capers.
- **A splash of lager** in place of white wine, and **lime, cilantro, and avocado**
  to finish instead of roasted pepper and peas alone.

## Make it yours

- **Sonora vs. Chihuahua:** cooks across the north argue the details — more or less
  tomato, potato in or out, beer or no beer. All are right.
- **Brown the chicken in lard** for the most traditional flavor (it's dairy-free).
- Add a spoonful of the tomato salsa's chiles for smokier heat, or keep the whole
  jalapeño in for aroma without the burn.
- Leftovers make a fantastic filling for tacos the next day.
